testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: While the shipped starting table routes (no Fit yet, as on a consumer's first runs), burnInProgress titles the section "burn-in ended: every starting Cell has its 20 merged PRs" but lists the cost guard's counts under it, for example 2, 0 and 1 of 20. The shipped plugin/scripts/router-table.json has burn_in:false, so the title follows the table's flag while the numbers come from a different source, and the view contradicts itself.
survived.evidence: In correctness/copy, `node probe1.mjs` called computeCellEvidence with table = validateTable(shipped router-table.json), fit {status:"missing"} and a guard with cells n 2, 0 and 1. It printed `source: starting table · no Fit yet: the next phase 0 writes one` and `burnIn: {"heading":"burn-in ended: every starting Cell has its 20 merged PRs","cells":[{"cell":"slow-high","n":2,"of":20},{"cell":"task-high","n":0,"of":20},{"cell":"smol-high","n":1,"of":20}]}`. `node -e` on router-table.json printed `false {"tripped":["smol-high"],"n":{"slow-high":104,"smol-high":32,"task-high":104}}`. The tests miss this: the starting-table test (compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs:580) uses DAY_ONE_TABLE with burn_in:true (tests/support/day-one-router-table.mjs:30), and the only `burn-in ended` assertion (test.mjs:606) uses a Fit whose counts are all at least 20.
survived.suggested_fix: Take the counts from the source that set the table's burn_in. While the starting table routes, use its own `guard.n`, the same way the Fit's own `guard.n` is used while the Fit routes; or stop titling 'burn-in ended' when the listed counts are short. Add a test that uses a burn_in:false starting table with a guard short of 20.

survived.claim: The new Cell evidence tab discards the catalog's read failure: when `omp models --json` fails, installFrom reports 'omp's model catalog not read yet' and the failure message appears nowhere in the policy model. A stale catalog whose latest refresh failed is also used silently as current. modelRoles has readLabel for both cases; the catalog has no equivalent.
survived.evidence: Probe via the test file's own fixtures (`fitted(...)` from tests/compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs, run as `node --test tests/zz-probe.test.mjs` in my copy). `catalog: {value:null, readAt:null, error:{at:1,message:'omp models --json failed (ENOENT)'}}` gave exploring 'exploring: not checked: omp's model catalog not read yet', and `JSON.stringify(policy).includes('ENOENT')` was false. `catalog: {...CATALOG, error:{at:2,message:'omp models --json failed (ETIMEDOUT)'}}` gave 'exploring task-xhigh, task-medium, slow-medium and smol-xhigh' with no mention of the failure, and includes('ETIMEDOUT') was false. In compute-cell-evidence.mjs, `catalog` is referenced only at lines 556-560 and 663-676, and `.error` is never read. A hung or broken `omp` therefore looks like 'not read yet' forever, and stale ladders look current.
survived.suggested_fix: Make installFrom word the catalog's failure the way readLabel does for modelRoles. Never-read plus error: 'omp's model catalog not read yet; reading fails: <message>'. Stale value plus error: carry an 'as read at …; reading fails: …' note on the exploring line. Pin both with tests.

survived.claim: When gather's readFitFile rejects a Fit that `route` accepts, the tab says 'the Fit is not read … starting table routes' and lays out the starting table, but `route` is routing by that Fit. The new view states which table routes; the old 'evidence favours' side only said 'no Fit read'.
survived.evidence: Probe `node --test tests/zz-probe2.test.mjs` wrote a router-fit.json with a valid table, then compared ticket-router's readFitBeside with board-gather's readFitFile. Missing `n_rows`: route uses Fit = true; tab read unreadable ('router table: `n_rows` is not a count'); tab source 'starting table · the Fit is not read: router table: `n_rows` is not a count'. Missing `computed_at`: route uses Fit = true; tab source says '`computed_at` is not a string'. Missing `tsv_blobs`: route uses Fit = true; tab source says '`tsv_blobs` is not an object'. readFitBeside (ticket-router.mjs:514-525) checks only validateTable(fit.table). The extra display-only checks in readFitFile are now treated as 'route falls back', and failedFitFlag says 'no Fit is read, so the starting table routes' on the same basis.
survived.suggested_fix: Do not let display-only fields (`computed_at`, `guard_computed_at`, `tsv_blobs`, `n_rows`) decide which table the tab says routes. Have the tab take the routing table from readFitBeside's accept/reject rule, and render the display fields as 'not checked' when they are malformed. Alternatively, reword the unreadable case so it does not claim the starting table routes.

votes.reason: Read the snapshot's code. readFitBeside (ticket-router.mjs:514-525) checks only validateTable(fit.table). readFitFile (board-gather.mjs:851-869) also requires computed_at and guard_computed_at to be strings, tsv_blobs to be an object, and table.n_rows to be a non-negative integer. validateTable never references n_rows. So a Fit missing any of those is routed by `route` but reported unreadable by gather, and the tab then says 'starting table · the Fit is not read: …'. I did not run the probe or the test suite. unverified.claim: readCatalog drops every catalog entry whose `thinking` is not an array. route's catalogEntry sees the unfiltered catalog. So for a modelRoles value written without its provider, the cockpit's installOf can match a different entry than route does, and the 'exploring …' Cells shown can differ from what route draws, against the PR's claim that they use 'the same functions route calls'.
unverified.evidence: `node -e` in correctness/copy, with catalog [{selector:"anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",thinking:null},{selector:"bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5",thinking:["low","medium","high"]}] and modelRoles {smol:"claude-haiku-4-5"}, printed `route {"smol":[],"task":[],"slow":[]}` and `cockpit {"smol":["low","medium","high"],"task":[],"slow":[]}`. With a provider-qualified role the two agree (probe1: both all-empty).
unverified.suggested_fix: Keep entries whose thinking is null and store them as `thinking: null`, so catalogEntry's first match is the same entry in both places. Only the `selector` and `thinking` fields need trimming to keep board.json small.

unverified.claim: The view now says it shows 'the table route routes by', but readFitFile is stricter than route's readFitBeside. A Fit file whose table validates but which lacks tsv_blobs (or string computed_at / guard_computed_at, or an integer n_rows) is shown as 'starting table · the Fit is not read', and the failed-Fit flag would say 'the starting table routes', while route actually routes by that Fit.
unverified.evidence: `node probe2.mjs` in correctness/copy, on a router-fit.json holding a valid table and no tsv_blobs, printed `cockpit readFitFile: {"status":"unreadable","why":"`tsv_blobs` is not an object"}` and `route readFitBeside: routes by the Fit's table`. metrics-refresh.mjs:315-318 always writes these fields, so this only happens with a hand-edited or partial file.
unverified.suggested_fix: Decide which table routes the same way readFitBeside does (validateTable on `table` alone). Treat missing metadata fields as 'not checked' labels instead of falling back to the starting table.

unverified.claim: fitView calls exploringWords(table, routed, s, inst) separately for each Objective, but the function takes no objective (it always dispatches the `cost` row), so the same stratum's string is computed again for every Objective. In addition, the `lines(o)` closure is followed by a second `.map` over each Objective's lines that only adds anchor/href, and the two passes can be one.
unverified.evidence: In my copy I replaced `lines(o)` plus the second `.map` with one `line(o, s, rest)` builder that sets stratum, groupOf, anchor and href, and memoized exploring in a Map keyed by stratum. `./agent-test` on 31 affected files: exit=0, tests 1642, pass 1642, fail 0. That run includes compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs, which asserts `lineOf(..., "cost", "*").exploring` and the anchors/hrefs, and cockpit-tabs.test.mjs.
unverified.suggested_fix: const exploring = new Map(); const exploringOf = (s) => { if (!exploring.has(s)) exploring.set(s, exploringWords(table, routed, s, inst)); return exploring.get(s); }; const line = (o, s, rest) => ({ stratum: s, ...groupOf(s), ...rest, anchor: `cells-row-${o}-${s}`, href: `#cells/row/${o}/${s}` }); then build each Objective's `lines` directly: table === null ? [line(o, "*", { entry: null, exploring: null, unread: … })] : Object.keys(table.rows[o]).map((s) => line(o, s, { entry: entry(o, s), exploring: exploringOf(s), unread: null })).

unverified.claim: The new readCatalog copies about eight lines of readModelRoles: the execRead spawn, the code/signal/exit `how` formatting, the `failed (…)` message, the JSON.parse with its `printed non-JSON` fallback, and `omp ${argv.join(" ")}` written out in three messages. A shared helper would leave each reader with only its shape check.
unverified.evidence: In my copy I added `async function readOmpJson(argv, timeout)` returning `{ ok: true, cmd, json }` or `{ ok: false, why }` with the same `why` strings, and rewrote readModelRoles (`r.json?.value`) and readCatalog (`r.json`) on top of it. board-cell-evidence-gather.test.mjs:126,130,165,169 assert the exact `printed non-JSON`, `printed no modelRoles record` and `printed no model list` strings. The 31-file run passed 1642/1642.
unverified.suggested_fix: async function readOmpJson(argv, timeout) { const cmd = `omp ${argv.join(" ")}`; const r = await execRead("omp", argv, { timeout }); if (r.error) { const how = r.code ?? (r.signal ? `killed by ${r.signal}` : `exit ${r.status}`); return { ok: false, why: `${cmd} failed (${how})` }; } try { return { ok: true, cmd, json: JSON.parse(r.stdout) }; } catch { return { ok: false, why: `${cmd} printed non-JSON` }; } } — then readCatalog becomes `const r = await readOmpJson(["models","--json"], timeout); if (!r.ok) return r; …shape check…`, and readModelRoles is rewritten the same way.
